lastCompletedStory.title: WARNING: Symmetric under-match: because `isSidecarArgv` now REQUIRES argv[0].st…

nextStoryContext: US-R2-002 closed the last known round-2 WARNING for CAM-482: isSidecarArgv's argv[0].startsWith('/') anchor (added in US-R1-001) was a SYMMETRIC under-match, not a fix. It excluded a legitimate live sidecar advertised under a bare, PATH-relative argv[0] (['cam','sidecar'], the shape every pre-US-002 binary spawns, and the shape hit during an operator's rebuild/reinstall upgrade window when a sidecar from the previous binary is still running with a stale/absent pid file) exactly as readily as it excluded an impostor -- and it never actually closed the false-positive hole it was added for, since the round-1 CRITICAL repro ('/usr/bin/tail -F sidecar') has an ABSOLUTE argv[0] and kept matching regardless throughout US-R1-001's own lifetime (only US-R2-001's separate process-identity check, holdsSidecarLogOpen, actually closed that hole). Fix: isSidecarArgv (src/commands/stop.ts) is back to a pure argv-shape quick filter -- `argv.length >= 2 && argv[argv.length-1] === 'sidecar'` -- with NO argv[0] anchor of any kind (no absolute-path requirement, no token-count check, per US-R1-002). matchesSidecarForProject is unchanged in signature (still composes isSidecarArgv with strict cwd equality). defaultListProcesses's process-identity check (holdsSidecarLogOpen, added US-R2-001) is untouched and remains the ONLY real defense against the false-positive direction -- verified unaffected by this change because the real-I/O integration test's decoy process (test/integration/stop-defaultlistprocesses-real.test.ts) already used an ABSOLUTE argv[0] and was excluded purely by NOT holding the sidecar log file open, never by argv[0] being non-absolute; that test was re-run green with no modification needed. Expanded isSidecarArgv's and defaultListProcesses's docstrings to state explicitly that argv shape (with or without a path-absoluteness requirement) can never discriminate a real self-spawn from an unrelated process that happens to echo the literal token 'sidecar' -- that job belongs entirely to the identity check one layer up -- as a GOTCHA against a future story re-adding any argv[0] shape requirement here. Test changes in test/stop-sidecar-fallback.test.ts: removed the now-inverted 'false-positive argv class (CAM-482)' describe block (its premise, that a bare-argv[0] command ending in 'sidecar' must NOT match at the pure argv+cwd layer, is no longer true by design and was never actually protective in production once the identity check existed) and replaced it with a 'bare argv[0] sidecar shape (CAM-482)' describe block proving a legitimate sidecar advertised under ['cam','sidecar'] IS matched again, closing the exact coverage gap the story's WARNING called out ('no test covers the bare-name shape any more'). test/commands/stop-name-agnostic.test.ts was NOT touched: none of its cases assert on argv[0] absoluteness as a rejection reason (case 4's rejection is driven by the last token not being 'sidecar', unaffected). File-size ceilings raised for the two files this story grew (src/commands/stop.ts 789->799, test/stop-sidecar-fallback.test.ts 196->213) per the established _ref dated-note convention; no other budgeted file touched. Full quality spine green: typecheck 0 errors, 5934 tests pass (0 fail), check:all (lint/file-size/debt-markers/version-skips/coverage/dead-code/dup/ci-parity/agents-md/test-sleeps/skip-ratchet) all ok. This closes the last known round-2 WARNING for CAM-482 that this agent is aware of from its spawn prompt; the next agent should re-verify against the current prd.json/review artifact whether any further round-2 findings remain open before assuming the round is fully clean.
